paragraphs: Here's what this whole passage says, friend: the Lord opens hearts, and He doesn't care who is holding the door. A businesswoman by the river hears Paul, and "The Lord opened her heart to respond to Paul’s message." (Acts 16:14) Then a jailer who is about to end his own life asks, "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?" (Acts 16:30) Two people who could not be more different, one story, and the same Lord doing the opening.

And look at the answer they get. "Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved, you and your household." (Acts 16:31) Nobody hands the jailer a to-do list or tells him to earn it. Salvation was never a cookie you bake your way into, friend, it's a gift, and the first thing that grows from it is JOY. His household was baptized and they rejoiced "that they had come to believe in God." (Acts 16:34)

Now check out Paul and Silas, because I think this is where it gets personal for you. They were beaten and locked in the inner cell, and at midnight they were "praying and singing hymns to God," while the other prisoners listened. (Acts 16:25) I believe somebody is always listening when you stay faithful in the dark. So when your night gets long, baker, keep praying, keep singing, and keep believing, because the Lord can open hearts around you, and maybe even the doors too.
